evidence: Plin. NH 28.23, on the custom: cūr sternuentēs salūtāmus?

terms.gloss: God bless you (in thanks or good wishes)
terms.grammar: optative subjunctive: “may the gods do well by you”
evidence: Ter. Ad. 5.7.20; Plaut. Pers. 4.3.18 (Lewis & Short), s.v. bene
Traupman p. 99: tibi dī bene faciant
terms.comment: Not the reply to a sneeze but a blessing in thanks: Lewis & Short, “may the gods bless you”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 94.
